summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, GERD, asthma, and tobacco use was admitted for shortness of breath and chest tightness. Initial evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism and cardiac ischemia. She was diagnosed with reactive airway disease and treated with a prednisone burst, albuterol nebulizers, and initiation of Symbicort. Her symptoms improved during the hospital stay. On the second day, she had a fall with head impact; CT head was normal, and lorazepam was reduced to minimize fall risk. She was discharged home with inhaler education, smoking cessation support, and plans for pulmonary follow-up and lung nodule surveillance. Chronic conditions were managed, and glycemic control was maintained with insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
